name: Question 7
problem:
Let $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ be a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Let $Y=2{X}_{1}+4{X}_{2}.$ Calculate $P(Y\le 10).$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5596\,$ | $\,0.5636\,$ | $\,0.5675\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.5987\,$ | $\,0.6026\,$ | $\,0.6064\,$ |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6368\,$ | $\,0.6406\,$ | $\,0.6443\,$ |
worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ is a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}{\mu }_{1} \\ {\mu }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & {\sigma }_{12} \\ {\sigma }_{21} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y=a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable for all values of $a$ and $b,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & =a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2}, \\ Var[Y] & ={a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+2ab{\sigma }_{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have ${\mu }_{1}=-2$ and ${\mu }_{2}=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =\text{E}[2{X}_{1}+4{X}_{2}] \\  & =2\text{E}[{X}_{1}]+4\text{E}[{X}_{2}] \\  & =2{\mu }_{1}+4{\mu }_{2} \\  & =2(-2)+4(3) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we have ${\sigma }_{1}^{2}=2,{\sigma }_{2}^{2}=4,$ and ${\sigma }_{12}={\sigma }_{21}=-1.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Var[Y] & =Var[2{X}_{1}+4{X}_{2}] \\  & ={2}^{2}(2)+{4}^{2}(4)+2(2)(4)(-1) \\  & =8+64-16 \\  & =56.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
Y∼N(8,56).
$$

Now, we need to compute $P(Y\le 10).$ First, transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 10) & =P(Z\le \frac{10-8}{\sqrt{56}}) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.27) \\  & =Φ(0.27)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.27)=0.6064.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(Y\le 10)=0.6064.
$$

E[Y]=aμ1+bμ2,Var[Y]=a2σ12+b2σ22+2abσ12.

In our case, we have μ1=−2 and μ2=3. Therefore, E[Y]=E[2X1+4X2]=2E[X1]+4E[X2]=2μ1+4μ2=2(−2)+4(3)=8.
